issues.legal_issue: A decree for specific performance that is affirmed on appeal merges into the appellate decree, which is the operative decree for execution.
material_facts: Both sides appealed the trial court’s decree for specific performance, and the appellate court dismissed both appeals while affirming the decree.
The decree-holder sought execution, and the judgment debtor objected that the balance had not been paid within the period stated in the trial court’s decree.
The appellate court decided the appeals before the decree-holder deposited the balance of the sale consideration.
issues.conclusion: The trial court’s decree merged into the appellate decree, and the decree-holder’s right to execute the appellate decree could not be defeated on the ground that the trial court’s payment period had elapsed.
issues.legal_principle: The doctrine of merger means that, after an appellate court decides a matter on the merits, its decree is the single operative decree, whether it affirms, modifies or reverses the decree below. The Court relied on Kunhayammed v State of Kerala, Chandi Prasad v Jagdish Prasad, Khoday Distilleries Ltd v Sri Mahadeshwara Sahakara Sakkare Karkhane Ltd, and Shanthi v T D Vishwanathan. Order 41 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that an appeal does not by itself stay execution, but that does not prevent merger when the appeal is decided.

predicates.specific_performance_execution: A party is seeking execution of a decree for specific performance.
predicates.appeal_decided_on_merits: An appellate court has decided an appeal concerning the decree on its merits.

issues.definition: When execution of a specific-performance decree is sought after an appeal concerning it has been decided on the merits, the appellate decree is the operative decree for execution.

issues.legal_issue: A court retains authority over a decree for specific performance to extend the time for compliance, and a prompt, bona fide payment after appellate confirmation need not defeat execution.
material_facts: The decree-holder had paid most of the sale consideration before the decree was made.
The trial court directed execution of the sale deed upon payment of the balance, but did not separately state a period for the decree-holder to make that payment.
The appellate court affirmed the decree, and the decree-holder deposited the balance about a month later.
The court found that the decree-holder had acted bona fide and that the equities favoured execution.
issues.conclusion: The delayed deposit did not render the decree inexecutable; the executing court was justified in rejecting the judgment debtor’s objections.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Specific Relief Act allows the court, on an application, to rescind a contract when the purchaser fails to comply with the decree, and also permits the court to extend the time for compliance. The court does not become functus officio after granting specific performance; the decree is in the nature of a preliminary decree, and the court retains jurisdiction until the sale deed is executed. The Court relied on Sardar Mohar Singh v Mangilal and Bhupinder Kumar v Angrej Singh. It distinguished V S Palanichamy Chettiar Firm v C Alagappan, where the delay was substantially longer and unexplained, and emphasised the decree-holder’s conduct and the circumstances of the case.

rule.if: specific_performance_execution and substantial_prior_payment and appeal_affirmed_decree and balance_paid_promptly_after_appeal

predicates.specific_performance_execution: A party is seeking execution of a decree for specific performance.
predicates.substantial_prior_payment: The decree-holder paid a substantial part of the agreed consideration before seeking execution.
predicates.appeal_affirmed_decree: An appellate court affirmed the specific-performance decree.
predicates.balance_paid_promptly_after_appeal: The decree-holder paid the remaining consideration soon after the appellate decision.

issues.definition: When a decree-holder seeking execution has already paid a substantial part of the consideration and promptly pays the balance after the decree is affirmed on appeal, the delay does not defeat execution.

issues.legal_issue: A court exercising revisional jurisdiction in an execution proceeding cannot replace a decree for specific performance with an order for refund.
material_facts: The executing court rejected the judgment debtor’s objections and allowed execution of the decree for specific performance.
In revision arising from that execution proceeding, the High Court set aside the executing court’s order and substituted a refund of money for specific performance.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its revisional jurisdiction by modifying the decree in the execution revision and substituting a refund for specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: A revisional court dealing with an execution proceeding cannot modify the underlying decree by substituting a different substantive remedy for the one granted. The Supreme Court held that the High Court’s course was not open in law.

predicates.civil_revision_from_execution_proceeding: A revision is brought against an order made in an execution proceeding.
predicates.revision_court_substitutes_different_rem: The revisional court replaces the remedy granted by the decree with a different remedy.

issues.definition: When a revisional court reviews an order in an execution proceeding, it cannot replace the remedy granted by the decree with a different one.
